name: NOISE1: is the stochastic world model's fork failure caused by WHERE its noise enters?
question: User poster question: did the stochastic (flow-matching) model fail because of the DINO latent or because of where its noise is added? The DINO part is answered by existing data (same latent for both models; the deterministic model on that latent catches forks; split test on real latent futures keeps 97% of forks). This test isolates noise placement with the SAME trained stochastic network (results/program_b/step3/wm_stochastic.pt), changing only how noise is drawn at test time.
data: the 60 held-out D0 states (results/program_b/step3/d0, 64 real futures each; 35 real-latent forks), the same states, actions, perturbed starts (diagnostics/pert_*.npz), seeds 20261060+n, readout (persistent_mode_alarm) and describe() as results/jenga/step3_diagnostics.json

variants.S_step: fresh independent noise per future per step (as published; true start)
variants.S_step_pert: fresh independent noise per future per step, perturbed starts
variants.S_shared: one noise draw per step SHARED by all 64 futures; futures differ only via their actions (true start)
variants.S_shared_pert: shared per-step noise, perturbed starts (futures differ only via actions + starts, as the deterministic model)
variants.S_zero: noise = 0 at every step (the flow's noise-free path), true start

metrics: per variant: forks caught = alarms on the 35 real-latent forks; false alarms = alarms on the 25 non-forks; spread ratio to real; main-axis (PC1) share on forks

decision_rule.placement: noise placement explains the failure if the better of S_shared_pert / S_zero_pert catches >= 2x the forks of S_step_pert AND is within 10 points of D_pert
decision_rule.dynamics: the stochastic network's own learned dynamics are (also) insensitive if both S_shared_pert and S_zero_pert stay within 10 points of S_step_pert

status: descriptive diagnostic on held-out TRAIN states (as step3_diagnostics); no model trained or selected; single GPU process
